newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa abolishes maize floor prices - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa abolishes maize floor prices - paper.

text.p: South African Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom on Thursday abolished maize floor prices and price stabilisation for farmers, Business Day newspaper said on Friday.
Hanekom said he had decided "after careful consideration and talks with a variety of role players", that a statutory floor price was "not desirable", the paper quoted him as saying.
There would be no marketing stabilisation levy for the 199/98 marketing year, it said.
Maize producers and co-operatives last Friday proposed at a meeting of industry representatives that a floor price of around 490 rand a tonne be fixed in the market from May next year.
But talks deadlocked when processors, traders and other maize buyers strongly opposed such an intervention and the agriculture minister was asked to make a ruling.

Hanekom on Thursday advised farmers who were concerned about the possibilty of low prices for the next harvest "to arrange forward contracts for a proportion of their crop and/or explore the possiblility of hedging their price risk on the Safex (South African Futures Exchange) agricultural markets division", the paper said.

South Africa's domestic maize market was freed of government intervention in May last year, although a levy still has to be paid by the industry. Government still plays a role in the export market, through the Maize Board, which fixes a minimum price.
